hazards.description: The road design facilitates higher vehicle speeds, increasing the risk of severe injury in the event of a collision.

hazards.name: Sightline obstructions from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb can hide pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers, especially at potential crossing points.

hazards.name: Sightline obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb can obscure pedestrians, especially children, from the view of approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located directly in the center of the narrow sidewalk on the left, forcing pedestrians to maneuver around them.
hazards.location_in_image: Left sidewalk along the row of brick buildings

hazards.name: Long Unprotected Crossing
hazards.description: The wide roadway width combined with a lack of midblock crossings or refuge islands creates a significant barrier for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Spanning the width of the roadway in the foreground

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parking
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along both sides of the street may obscure sight lines between pedestrians and approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: A line of parked cars obscures the view between the sidewalk and the travel lane, making it difficult for drivers to see pedestrians who might step into the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line in the foreground and middle ground.

hazards.name: Lack of Mid-block Crossings
hazards.description: There are no marked crossings visible for a long stretch, which may lead to unsafe mid-block crossing attempts.

hazards.name: Wide Curb Cuts
hazards.description: Multiple wide vehicle access points across the sidewalk increase the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflicts.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and left-center background where parking lots meet the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along both curbs obstruct sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the travel lanes.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both sides of the roadway

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Driveway Access
hazards.description: A wide driveway or alleyway between buildings creates a conflict point where vehicles may cross the pedestrian path.
hazards.location_in_image: The gap between the two red brick buildings in the center.

hazards.name: Frequent Driveway Conflict Points
hazards.description: Large curb cuts for parking lots and driveways on the left side of the image create multiple points where vehicles may cross the pedestrian path unexpectedly.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image along the sidewalk

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Visibility
hazards.description: Parked vehicles and the lack of curb extensions may obscure pedestrians from the view of oncoming traffic if they attempt to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side where white vans are parked near the sidewalk edge

hazards.name: Wide Roadway Geometry
hazards.description: The excessive width of the roadway, including a wide painted median, encourages higher vehicle speeds and increases pedestrian exposure time during crossings.

hazards.name: Lack of Mid-block Crossing
hazards.description: In a mixed-use area with destinations on both sides, the absence of marked crossings forces pedestrians to cross at unprotected locations.

hazards.name: Uneven Pavement
hazards.description: Cracked and uneven concrete slabs across the wide pedestrian area create tripping hazards.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the foreground and middle ground paved area

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from large vehicles
hazards.description: The large truck in the foreground obscures sightlines between pedestrians and other drivers approaching the intersection.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb can block the visibility of pedestrians attempting to cross the street.

hazards.name: Poor Pavement Condition
hazards.description: The sidewalk surface appears uneven and cracked, posing a potential trip hazard.

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crossings with high-visibility paint to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb extensions
interventions.description: Implement bulb-outs at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street trees and landscaping
interventions.description: Add a line of street trees to provide a vertical buffer, improve the pedestrian experience, and naturally encourage slower driving speeds.

interventions.title: Midblock Pedestrian Crossing
interventions.description: Install a marked crosswalk with a pedestrian refuge island to reduce crossing distance and exposure.

interventions.title: Driveway Consolidation and Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of the commercial driveway to the minimum necessary for vehicle access, clearly defining the pedestrian path.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Add a planting strip or furniture zone between the sidewalk and the roadway to provide a physical buffer and improve the pedestrian environment.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Construct a raised refuge island within the existing painted median to provide a safe waiting area for pedestrians mid-crossing.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Adding street trees would provide a vertical buffer between the sidewalk and the street while improving the pedestrian experience.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Midblock Crossing
interventions.description: Install a marked crosswalk with high-visibility paint and a pedestrian refuge island to break up the crossing distance.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Paving and Completion
interventions.description: Pave the dirt area on the left side to provide a continuous, ADA-compliant walkway.

interventions.title: High-visibility crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a marked crossing with high-visibility paint and signage to alert drivers to the presence of pedestrians.

interventions.title: Protected Bike Lane
interventions.description: Install physical barriers like bollards or a raised curb to separate the bike lane from motor vehicle traffic.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Planting street trees would provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions at potential crossing points to shorten crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Green Infrastructure
interventions.description: Add a line of street trees to provide a physical buffer, reduce the perceived width of the road to slow traffic, and improve the walking environment.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add dedicated pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve visibility and safety during nighttime hours, especially along the vacant lot.

interventions.title: Street Furniture and Landscaping
interventions.description: Enhance the sidewalk area with benches or additional planters to activate the space in front of the vacant lot.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Mid-block Crossing
interventions.description: Implement a marked mid-block crossing with a pedestrian refuge island and potentially an RRFB to provide a safe legal crossing point.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffer/Planting Strip
interventions.description: Install a furniture zone or planting strip with street trees to provide physical and psychological separation between pedestrians and moving vehicles.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crossing with Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a marked mid-block crossing with a pedestrian refuge island and high-visibility signage or RRFBs to facilitate safer crossings.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Mid-block Crosswalk
interventions.description: Implement a marked crosswalk with high-visibility paint and appropriate signage to provide a designated and safer crossing point.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Introduce speed humps or raised tables to reduce vehicle speeds along this wide, straight section of the street.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer
interventions.description: Add a planting strip or furniture zone to provide physical separation from traffic and improve the walking environment.

interventions.title: Mid-block Pedestrian Crossing
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk with a pedestrian refuge island in the center median to break up the crossing distance.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Repair
interventions.description: Level and repair the concrete slabs to ensure a smooth, accessible surface for all users.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles receive a green light, reducing turning conflicts.

interventions.title: Midblock Crossing with Refuge
interventions.description: Add a marked midblock crosswalk with a pedestrian refuge island to provide a safe point for crossing the wide street.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening and Obstruction Removal
interventions.description: Widen the sidewalk and relocate utility poles to the furniture zone to ensure a clear, accessible path of travel.
